exercises.title: What does this code do?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick what it does.
options: Counts the words in a line of text
Parses a list of numbers separated by spaces
Splits text into a name and a number, or None
exercises.explanation: It takes the first two words, parses the second one as a number, and gives `None` if a word is missing or is not a number.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick the output.
exercises.explanation: 7 is odd, so the first guard fails. The second guard `x > 5` is true, so the arm prints `big odd 7`.

exercises.title: What does this function do?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick what it does.
options: Counts the items of the slice
Names the shape of a slice
Checks that a slice is sorted
exercises.explanation: It matches the slice by its shape (empty, one item, equal first and last items, or anything else) and returns a word for each.

exercises.title: Why does it not compile?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick the cause.
options: `Yellow` is not handled by the match
exercises.explanation: A `match` must cover every variant. Add a `Light::Yellow` arm, or a `_` arm, and it compiles.
